intro: Welcome to Miletus, an ancient city in Aydın province whose story reaches back to the 15th century BC. This was a harbour city, and a remarkable one: here grid-plan urbanism was born, and here philosophy took its first steps.
history: Imagine a city with not one harbour but four. From them Miletus dominated Mediterranean trade and founded over 90 colonies. Then the Persians destroyed it. Yet the city rose again, rebuilt on the grid plan of Hippodamus.
structure-1: You are now in front of the Great Theatre, one of the largest theatres in Anatolia. Its cavea, nearly 140 m across, opens like a stadium set against the hillside. Greek architects built it in 250-225 BC; under Rome, in AD 68-96, it was rebuilt with a three-storey stone stage building. That front still survives, with the workshops behind it, and it is among the most complete anywhere.
structure-4: Now to the North Agora, the colonnaded commercial square in the north of the city. Picture merchants and buyers bargaining in the shade of its columns.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the Baths of Faustina, the Bouleuterion and the İlyas Bey Mosque.
facts: Did you know? The city now lies 8 km inland: the Meander river filled in all four of its harbours. The theatre held 15,000 people and is among the largest in the Aegean, and in the front row you can still see the sockets for the emperor's box. Thales, Anaximander and Anaximenes all came from here — the first three names in Western philosophy shared one harbour. And the monumental Market Gate? It was shipped piece by piece to Berlin in 1907-08 and re-erected there.
outro: Our journey through Miletus ends here. Please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. Thank you for walking with us, and enjoy your visit.
